title: 2021 AMC 12B Problem 16
statement: Let \(g(x)\) be a polynomial with leading coefficient \(1,\) whose three roots are the reciprocals of the three roots of \(f(x)=x^3+ax^2+bx+c,\) where \(1\lt a\lt b\lt c.\) What is \(g(1)\) in terms of \(a,\) \(b,\) and \(c?\)

solutions.text:
Let \(f\) have roots \(r,s,t.\) Since \(g\) is monic with roots \(\tfrac1r,\tfrac1s,\tfrac1t,\) \[ \begin{aligned} g(1) &= \left(1-\tfrac1r\right)\left(1-\tfrac1s\right) \\ &\quad {}\cdot \left(1-\tfrac1t\right) \\ &= \dfrac{(r-1)(s-1)(t-1)}{rst}. \end{aligned} \]

Now \(f(1)=(1-r)(1-s)(1-t)\) \(=1+a+b+c,\) so \((r-1)(s-1)(t-1)\) \(=-(1+a+b+c).\) Also \(rst=-c.\)

Therefore \(g(1)\) \(=\dfrac{-(1+a+b+c)}{-c}\) \(=\dfrac{1+a+b+c}{c}.\)

Thus, the correct answer is A.
hints: This equals \(\dfrac{(r-1)(s-1)(t-1)}{rst};\) relate the numerator to \(f(1)\) and the denominator to \(c\)
